findings.title: Async legacy writes inherit the request context and are cancelled when the request returns
findings.body: Each background goroutine builds its context with `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)`, where `ctx` is the incoming request context. The handler returns right after starting the goroutine, and the apiserver then cancels that request context. The legacy Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection calls will therefore often fail with `context canceled` before they finish, so legacy storage silently drifts out of sync. The same pattern is at lines 110, 135 and 163. The parent should be `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` so logger values are kept but cancellation is not.

findings.title: Legacy write failures in background goroutines are never logged
findings.body: The goroutines only record a duration metric with an error flag. They never log the error from the legacy Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection call. The previous code logged legacy failures. Now a failed safety write to legacy storage leaves no diagnostic trace beyond a counter, which makes divergence between the two stores hard to investigate.

findings.title: Storage create failure is recorded as a legacy metric
findings.body: When `d.Storage.Create` fails, the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)` instead of `recordStorageDuration`. Unified-storage errors are therefore reported as legacy errors, and storage error metrics are missing. Update has the same mistake at line 129.

findings.title: Legacy DeleteCollection result recorded as storage metric
findings.body: The background goroutine runs `d.Legacy.DeleteCollection` but records the result with `d.recordStorageDuration`. Legacy latency and errors are attributed to unified storage, which skews both metric series.

findings.title: Delete success metric uses object name as the kind label
findings.body: `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)` passes the object `name` where every other call passes `options.Kind`. This produces wrong labels and unbounded label cardinality, since there is one series per object name.

findings.title: Delete attaches the base logger to the context instead of the enriched one
findings.body: Delete builds `log` with name, kind and method, but then calls `klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)`. Downstream code that pulls the logger from the context loses those fields. Every other method uses `log` here.

findings.title: Legacy update reapplies the raw objInfo instead of the result from unified storage
findings.body: The old code wrapped the unified-storage result in `updateWrapper` so legacy received exactly the stored object. The new code passes the original `objInfo` to `Legacy.Update` asynchronously. `UpdatedObject` is then re-evaluated against legacy's own current object. For patch or apply requests this can produce a different result, and resourceVersion preconditions may fail. It also reuses a request-scoped `objInfo` after the request has completed.

findings.title: Request object shared with background goroutine while the handler continues using it
findings.body: `obj` (and `options`) are handed to a goroutine that calls `d.Legacy.Create`, while the apiserver keeps processing and serializing the response, which may reference the same object returned by storage. Legacy create implementations may mutate the object, for example by setting metadata. This creates a data race. A deep copy (`obj.DeepCopyObject()`) should be passed to the goroutine.

findings.title: Mode 3 integration tests check legacy reads immediately after async writes, so they are racy
findings.body: `doPlaylistTests` creates, updates and deletes through the k8s API, then immediately checks `/api/playlists` and `getFromBothAPIs` for matching legacy results. In mode 3 the legacy writes happen in a goroutine with no synchronization. These assertions can therefore run before legacy has been updated, making the new mode 3 file and unified test cases flaky.

findings.title: Unit tests never verify the async legacy writes
findings.body: The mode 3 Create, Update, Delete and DeleteCollection tests do not wait for the background goroutine and do not assert that the legacy store was called. Goroutines may also outlive the test. Legacy store and storage share one mock, so legacy calls silently match the storage expectations. Bugs in the legacy path, such as the context cancellation issue, go undetected.

findings.title: Duplicated go.work.sum entry
findings.body: The line `github.com/grafana/grafana/pkg/apimachinery v0.0.0-20240701135906-559738ce6ae1/go.mod` is added again even though it already appears a few lines above. The go.work.sum changes look like unrelated local churn that should not be in this PR.
